slides.title: Repeated trials and the law of large numbers
bullets: Lecture 04
Bernoulli trials and the binomial distribution
Waiting for a success: the geometric distribution
Running averages and the law of large numbers

slides.title: Bernoulli trials
bullets: A Bernoulli trial has two outcomes: success with probability p, failure with 1 − p.
In repeated trials, the trials are independent and every trial has the same p.
Indicator: I = 1 on success and I = 0 on failure, so E[I] = p.
Var(I) = p(1 − p), which is largest when p = 1/2.

slides.title: Counting successes
bullets: X = the number of successes in n independent trials, each with success probability p.
Any one sequence with k successes has probability p^k (1 − p)^(n − k).
There are C(n, k) such sequences: choose which k trials succeed.
So X takes the values 0, 1, …, n.

slides.title: The binomial distribution
bullets: X ~ Bin(n, p) means P(X = k) = C(n, k) p^k (1 − p)^(n − k) for k = 0, 1, …, n.
The probabilities add up to 1 by the binomial theorem.
Bin(1, p) is a single Bernoulli trial.
The shape: symmetric when p = 1/2, skewed when p is near 0 or 1.

slides.title: Mean and variance
bullets: Write X = I_1 + I_2 + ⋯ + I_n, one indicator per trial.
Linearity of expectation: E[X] = p + p + ⋯ + p = np.
Independence: the variances add, so Var(X) = np(1 − p).
The standard deviation √(np(1 − p)) grows like √n, not like n.

slides.title: Three examples
bullets: Fair coin, 10 flips: P(exactly 5 heads) = 252/1024 ≈ 0.246.
Shooter with p = 0.8, 5 shots: P(all 5 go in) = 0.8⁵ ≈ 0.328.
20 parts, each defective with probability 0.05: P(none defective) = 0.95²⁰ ≈ 0.358.
In each case: identify n and p, check independence, then use the formula.

slides.title: Waiting for the first success
bullets: T = the number of trials up to and including the first success.
E[T] = 1/p: a fair die needs 6 rolls on average to show a six.
Memoryless: past failures do not change the wait that is still ahead.

slides.title: Running averages
bullets: After n trials the running proportion of successes is X/n = (I_1 + ⋯ + I_n)/n.
E[X/n] = p and Var(X/n) = p(1 − p)/n.
The spread of the proportion shrinks like 1/√n.

slides.title: The law of large numbers
bullets: For every ε > 0: P(|X/n − p| ≥ ε) → 0 as n → ∞.
In words: the running proportion settles near p.
The count X does not settle near np: |X − np| typically grows like √n.

slides.title: Due for a win?
bullets: Independent trials have no memory: a streak does not change the next trial.
Early streaks are not corrected; they are diluted by later trials.
The law is about proportions, not about counts evening out.

slides.title: Summary
bullets: Bin(n, p): P(X = k) = C(n, k) p^k (1 − p)^(n − k), mean np, variance np(1 − p).
Geometric waiting time: P(T = k) = (1 − p)^(k − 1) p, mean 1/p.
Running proportions settle near p; streaks are diluted, never corrected.
